pp:me:2004:q16.title: GATE ME 2004 | Set 1 | Question: 16
pp:me:2004:q16.question: One dimensional unsteady state heat transfer equation for a sphere with heat generation at the rate of 'q' can be written as
options: $\frac{1}{r}\frac{\partial }{\partial r}\left ( r \frac{\partial T}{\partial r} \right )+\frac{q}{k}=\frac{1}{\alpha }\frac{\partial T}{\partial t}$

detailed_solution.markdown:
The one dimensional time dependent heat conduction equation can be written  more compactly as a simple equation,

$\frac{1}{r^{n}}\frac{\partial }{\partial r}\left ( r^{n} \frac{\partial T}{\partial r} \right )+\frac{q}{k}=\frac{\rho c}{k }\frac{\partial }{\partial t}$

where,

n = 0, For rectangular coordinates

n = 1, For cylindrical coordinates

n = 2, For spherical coordinates

Further, while using rectangular coordinates it is customary to replace the r-variable by the x-variable.

For sphere, substitute r = 2 in above equation

$\frac{1}{r^{2}}\frac{\partial }{\partial r}\left ( r^{2} \frac{\partial T}{\partial r} \right )+\frac{q}{k}=\frac{\rho c}{k }\frac{\partial }{\partial t}$

$\frac{1}{r^{2}}\frac{\partial }{\partial r}\left ( r^{2} \frac{\partial T}{\partial r} \right )+\frac{q}{k}=\frac{1}{\alpha }\frac{\partial }{\partial t}$

as $\alpha =\frac{k}{\rho c}=\text{thermal diffusivity}$

detailed_solution.markdown: Work output during the cycle $$\begin{aligned} &=m c_{p}\left(T_{3}-T_{2}\right)-m c_{p}\left(T_{4}-T_{1}\right) \\ &=m c_{p}\left(T_{3}-T_{4}\right)-m c_{p}\left(T_{2}-T_{1}\right) \\ &=m c_{p}\left[T_{3}\left(1-\frac{T_{4}}{T_{3}}\right)-T_{1}\left(\frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}-1\right)\right] \end{aligned}$$ since $\frac{T_{3}}{T_{4}}=\frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}=\left(r_{p}\right) \frac{\gamma-1}{\gamma} \quad\left(\text { Let } \frac{\gamma-1}{\gamma}=x, m c_{p}=K\right)$ $\therefore$ Work/cycle $=K\left[T_{3}\left(1-\frac{1}{r_{p}^{x}}\right)-T_{1}\left(r_{p}^{x}-1\right)\right]$ For maximum power, differentiate with respect to $r_{p}$ $$\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \quad \frac{d W}{d r_{p}}&=K\left[T_{3} \times \frac{x}{r_{p}(x+1)}-T_{1} \times r_{p}^{(x-1)}\right]=0 \\ &\qquad (For max.)\\ \Rightarrow \frac{x T_{3}}{r_{p}(x+1)}&=T_{1} \times\left(r_{p}\right)^{x-1} \\ \Rightarrow \quad r_{p}^{2 x}&=\frac{T_{3}}{T_{1}} \\ \therefore \quad r_{p}&=\left(\frac{T_{3}}{T_{1}}\right)^{\frac{1}{2 x}} \\ \text{or }\quad r_{p}&=\left(\frac{T_{\max }}{T_{\min }}\right)^{\frac{\gamma}{2(\gamma-1)}} \end{aligned}$$

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} &a_{x}=u \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}+v \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}+w \frac{\partial u}{\partial z}+\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}\\ &\therefore \quad a_{x}=u \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}\\ &Q=A u \end{aligned}$$ $$\begin{aligned} \text{or }\quad u&=\frac{Q}{A} \\ u&=\frac{Q}{\pi \mathrm{R}^{2}} \\ R &= R_{1}+\frac{R_{2}-R_{1}}{L} \cdot x \\ let,\\ R_{1}&=a\text{ and } \frac{R_{2}-R_{1}}{L}=b \\ \therefore \quad R&=a+b x \\ u &=\frac{Q}{\pi(a+b x)^{2}} \\ \frac{\partial u}{\partial x} &=\frac{-2 b Q}{\pi(a+b x)^{3}} \\ a_{x} &=u \frac{\partial u}{\partial x} \\ a_{x=L} &=\left.u \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}\right|_{x=L} \end{aligned}$$ and also replacing a and b $a_{x=L}=\frac{-2 Q^{2}\left(R_{1}-R_{2}\right)}{\pi^{2} L R_{2}^{5}}$

pp:me:2004:q48.title: GATE ME 2004 | Set 1 | Question: 48
pp:me:2004:q48.question: A closed cylinder having a radius R and height H is filled with oil density $\rho$. If the cylinder is rotated about its axis at an angular velocity of  $\omega$, the thrust at the bottom of the cylinder is

detailed_solution.markdown: We know that $$\begin{aligned} \frac{\partial p}{\partial r}&=\frac{\rho v^{2}}{r}=\rho \omega^{2} r \\ \Rightarrow \quad \int_{0}^{p} \partial p&=\int_{0}^{f} \rho \omega^{2} r d r\\ \therefore \quad p&=\frac{\rho \omega^{2} r^{2}}{2} \end{aligned}$$ Area of circular ring$=2 \pi r d r$ Force on elementary ring = Intensity of pressure x Area of ring $=\frac{\rho}{2} \omega^{2} r^{2} 2 \pi r d r$ $\therefore$ Total force on the bottom of the cylinder due to rotation $$\begin{aligned} \int_{0}^{R} \frac{\rho \omega^{2} r^{2}}{2} \cdot 2 \pi r d r &=\frac{\rho}{2} \omega^{2} \cdot 2 \pi \int_{0}^{R} r^{3} d r \\ &=\pi \omega^{2} \rho\left[\frac{r^{4}}{4}\right]_{0}^{R} \\ &=\rho \omega^{2} \cdot \frac{\pi R^{4}}{4} \end{aligned}$$ Thrust at the bottom of the cylinder = weight of water in cylinder or force due to hydrostatic pressure + total force on the top of cylinder due to rotation $$\begin{aligned} &=\rho g \times \pi R^{2} \times H+\rho \omega^{2} \times \frac{\pi R^{4}}{4} \\ &=\pi R^{2}\left[\frac{\rho \omega^{2} R^{2}}{4}+\rho g H\right] \end{aligned}$$

pp:me:2004:q49.title: GATE ME 2004 | Set 1 | Question: 49
pp:me:2004:q49.question:
For air flow over a flat plate, velocity (U) and boundary layer thickness ($\delta$) can be expressed respectively, as
$\frac{U}{U_{a}}=\frac{3}{2}\frac{y}{\delta }-\frac{1}{2}\left ( \frac{y}{\delta } \right )^{3}; \delta =\frac{4.64x}{\sqrt{Re_{x}}}$
If the free stream velocity is 2m/s, and air has kinematic viscosity of $1.5\times 10^{-5}m^{2}/s$ and density of $1.23 kg/m^{3}$, the wall shear stress at x = 1m, is

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics - Viscous, Turbulent Flow and Boundary Layer Theory
detailed_solution.markdown:
Reynold number

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Re}_{x}=\frac{u_{\infty} x}{u}=\frac{2 \times 1}{1.5 \times 10^{-5}}=1.33 \times 10^{5} \\ \delta=\frac{4.64 x}{\sqrt{\mathrm{Re}_{x}}}=\frac{4.64 \times 1}{\sqrt{1.33 \times 10^{5}}}=0.0127 \end{aligned}$$

$\text{Now, }\frac{d u}{d y}=u_{\infty}\left[\frac{3}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{\delta}-\frac{3}{2}\left(\frac{y^{2}}{\delta^{3}}\right)\right]$

Now, shear stress,

$$\begin{aligned} \tau_{0} &=\mu\left(\frac{d u}{d y}\right)_{y=0}=\mu \times \frac{3 u_{\infty}}{2 \delta} \\ &=\frac{3 u_{\infty} \times v \times \rho}{2 \delta} \quad \because \mu=v \rho \\ &=\frac{3 \times 2 \times 1.5 \times 10^{-5} \times 1.23}{2 \times 0.0127} \\ &=4.36 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{N} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{aligned}$$

pp:me:2004:q50.title: GATE ME 2004 | Set 1 | Question: 50
pp:me:2004:q50.question: A centrifugal pump is required to pump water to an open water tank situated 4 km away from the location of the pump through a pipe of diameter 0.2 m having Darcy's friction factor of 0.01. The average speed of water in the pipe is 2 m/s. If it is maintain a constant head of 5 m in the tank, neglecting other minor losses, the absolute discharge pressure at the pump exit is

$$\begin{aligned} l &=4 \mathrm{km}=4000 \mathrm{m} \\ d &=0.2 \mathrm{m} \\ f &=0.01 \\ V &=2 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \\ h &=5 \mathrm{m} \\ h_{f} &=\frac{f l V^{2}}{2 g d}=\frac{0.01 \times 4000 \times(2)^{2}}{2 \times 9.81 \times 0.2} \\ &=40.77 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}$$

Head produced by the pump,

Absolute discharge pressure at the pump exit

detailed_solution.markdown: Given data: $$\begin{aligned} \eta &=70 \%=0.70 \\ (\mathrm{COP})_{R} &=5 \\ Q_{3} &=? \\ Q_{1} &=1 \mathrm{kJ} \end{aligned}$$ For heat engine, $$\begin{aligned} \eta &=1-\frac{Q_{2}}{Q_{1}} \\ 0.70 &=1-\frac{Q_{2}}{1}\\ \text{or } \quad Q_{2}&=0.3 \mathrm{kJ} \\ W &=Q_{1}-Q_{2}=1-0.3 \\ &=0.7 \mathrm{kJ}\\ \text{For refrigerator,}\\ (\mathrm{COP})_{\mathrm{R}} &=\frac{Q_{3}}{W} \\ 5 &=\frac{Q_{3}}{0.7} \\ \text{or}\quad Q_{3} &=0.7 \times 5=3.5 \mathrm{kJ} \end{aligned}$$

pp:me:2004:q52.title: GATE ME 2004 | Set 1 | Question: 52

A solar collector receiving solar radiation at the rate of 0.6 $kW/m^{2}$

detailed_solution.markdown: Given data: $Q=0.6 \mathrm{kW} / \mathrm{m}^{2}$ Overall efficiency of the fluid system, $$\begin{aligned} \eta_{\text {fluid }} &=50 \%=0.50 \\ T_{1} &=350 \mathrm{K} \\ T_{2} &=313 \mathrm{K} \\ W &=2.5 \mathrm{kW} \end{aligned}$$ Overall efficiency of the fluid system, $$\begin{aligned} \eta_{\text {fluid }} &=\frac{Q_{1}}{Q} \\ 0.50 &=\frac{Q_{1}}{0.6} \\ \text{or}\qquad Q_{1}&=0.05\times 0.6=0.3 \mathrm{kW} / \mathrm{m}^{2}\\ \end{aligned}$$ Let A= Minimum area of the solar collector $\therefore Q_{1}=0.3 \mathrm{A} \mathrm{kW}$ For minimum area of the solar collector, the heat engine is reversible $\therefore$ Thermal efficiency, $$\begin{aligned} \eta &=1-\frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}} \\ &=1-\frac{313}{350}=1-0.895=0.105 \\ \text { also } \quad \eta &=\frac{W}{Q_{1}} \\ \therefore \qquad 0.105 &=\frac{2.5}{0.3 A} \\ A &=79.36 \mathrm{m}^{2} \\ & \end{aligned}$$
